It does not add\n`POST /route/task`, a second score function, or a second routing decision store.\nThe existing `selected.vendor/model/endpoint_kind` meaning remains observable and\nunchanged; assignment and provenance are additive fields.\n\n## D2 — Preserve compatibility with an optional strict profile\n\nLegacy `task_signals` remains accepted with its current permissive extra-field\nbehavior because existing phase callers send fields such as `write_allow`. A new\noptional `routing_profile` is strict (`extra=forbid`) and types:\n\n- expected duration seconds;\n- scope category (`read-only|bounded-write|broad-write`);\n- interactivity (`interactive|headless`);\n- secret need category (`none|brokered|direct`), never a secret value;\n- positive parallelism;\n- repository shape (`single-package|monorepo|unknown`);\n- roadmap-policy constraints (allowed/excluded lane/vendor sets and an allowed-location set);\n- optional required location, isolation, and dispatch mode.\n\nPydantic validates the external boundary and FastAPI/MCP share the same request model.\nNew response objects are optional-with-default for legacy validation but are always\npopulated by a successful DG-04 service decision.\n\n## D3 — Rules are ordered, typed, and versioned\n\n`agent-coordinator/routing.yaml` carries `schema_version`, `policy_version`,\ndispatch-mode defaults, ordered first-match constraint rules, and a local-fallback\ndimension table. A dedicated loader validates unknown fields, duplicate IDs, enum values,\nranges, and phase dispatch defaults, then records a SHA-256 checksum of canonical file\nbytes.\n\nEach rule has a typed `when` predicate over the profile and a typed `constrain` block for\nlocation, isolation, and dispatch mode. Explicit request constraints take precedence;\notherwise the first matching rule that mentions a dimension constrains that dimension.\nThe phase-specific or global dispatch default is used only when no explicit or rule-based\ndispatch mode exists; unmatched location/isolation remain unconstrained. Rules narrow\nfeasibility and never add a second utility score. Changing a rule therefore changes the\nfeasible assignment set without code edits.\n\nThe Docker image copies the file beside `agents.yaml` and the loader resolves it from\n`ROUTING_CONFIG` or the package root, never the process working directory.\n\n## D4 — DG-01 is the only lane source and joins are exact\n\n`RoutingService` injects/loads `VendorRegistryService` in process and requests all\nlanes without `available_only` prefiltering so exclusion provenance is retained. For\neach lane it consumes dg-01's projected catalog models. It forms an assignment only when\nthe catalog candidate identity exactly equals the projection key:\n\n`(catalog_vendor, model, endpoint_kind, base_url)`.\n\n`base_url` and additive lane identity travel through `CandidateInput` and\n`ScoredCandidate`. Agent-name suffixes, provider/publisher guesses, substring matches,\nand fuzzy model names are forbidden. Missing or ambiguous projections remain explicit\nregistry misses and never become routable candidates.\n\nA watchdog `ConfiguredCatalogSync` job materializes configured non-OpenRouter lane\nmodels in `model_catalog`. `agents.yaml` explicitly sets `catalog_vendor` and\n`endpoint_kind` for those lanes: local subscription CLIs use their exact vendor type plus\n`vendor-cli`; remote SDK lanes use their exact vendor type plus `vendor-sdk`. CLI model\nIDs come from the canonical provider model map; SDK model IDs come only from the lane's\nSDK model/fallback list. The job inserts only missing identity rows, with enabled catalog\navailability and unknown price/posterior, and never overwrites existing pricing,\nposterior, availability, or refresh data. Registry probe/rate-limit state remains the live\nlane-availability source.\n\nOpenRouter/local catalog rows remain owned by their existing refresh/probe jobs; for a\nmulti-publisher OpenRouter lane, exact model/endpoint/base-URL matching must yield one row\nbefore the row's catalog vendor becomes part of the four-field key. Missing or ambiguous\nidentity metadata is an explicit configuration miss, never filled from an agent-name\nsuffix or publisher guess. A real-agents.yaml test proves at least one configured CLI\nlane projects exactly after this bootstrap.\n\nThe routing path constructs a read-only `VendorRegistryService(audit=None)` because the\nrouter persists its own typed exclusions and atomic audit link; this avoids emitting one\ngeneric projection-miss audit row per request. The registry and catalog snapshots are\neach loaded once per request. A registry read or shape failure fails closed as\n`routing-registry-unavailable`; it never falls back to catalog-only scoring. Catalog rows\nwith no exact configured lane projection are retained in `excluded` as\n`catalog:no-configured-lane`, rather than disappearing silently.\n\n## D5 — Feasibility precedes DG-00 utility\n\nFor each exact lane/model pair, pure feasibility checks apply in deterministic order:\n\n1. live lane availability and lane/model rate limits;\n2. dispatchability, archetype, and requested/default dispatch mode;\n3. explicit/configured location and isolation constraints;\n4. roadmap-policy allow/exclude sets;\n5. catalog availability and dg-00 modality/quota constraints.\n\nReasons are machine-readable and sanitized. DG-00's existing `unavailable` and\n`quota:exhausted` values remain accepted alongside DG-04's namespaced reasons. Only feasible lane/model candidates enter\nthe existing `score_and_rank`; DG-04 does not duplicate quality, posterior, cost,\nlatency, headroom, or exploration math. Multiple lanes may project the same catalog\nmodel, so the final stable order is `(-score, agent_id, catalog identity)`.\nLocation and isolation constraints use exact equality and dispatch mode uses exact\nmembership in the lane's configured modes; DG-04 does not infer an isolation-strength\nordering.\n\n## D6 — Assignment and provenance are additive\n\nA successful response adds top-level:\n\n- `assignment`: exact `agent_id`, `vendor_type`, `policy_vendor`,\n  `catalog_vendor`, location, isolation, dispatch mode, model, endpoint kind, and base\n  URL;\n- `provenance`: source (`coordinator` or `local-static`), policy version/checksum,\n  matched rule IDs, rationale, persistence flag, durable-audit flag, and exact\n  lane/catalog key.\n\nThe selected candidate and every alternative carry their own additive `assignment`, while\nthe response retains the selected candidate's assignment/provenance at top level for\nconvenience. Existing selected-candidate fields remain intact for older consumers.\nExcluded assignments use a typed shape containing lane/catalog identity and a bounded\nmachine-readable reason.\n\n## D7 — Durable routing record is authoritative; audit event is linked\n\nThe existing `routing_decisions` row is the authoritative durable routing audit. Its\nsanitized `request` stores only declared task signals and the strict routing profile;\npermissive legacy extras such as `write_allow` are never persisted. Its `selected` object\nstores selected assignment plus provenance, and every item in `alternatives` stores its\nown assignment. `excluded` stores typed exclusion records. These are additive JSONB\nshapes and require no new table columns.\n\nMigration `042_atomic_routing_audit.sql` adds one transaction-scoped RPC that inserts the\n`routing_decisions` row and a sanitized link-only `routing_decision` audit-log event\natomically. The event contains only decision ID, selected agent/model, routing-policy\nversion/checksum, source, and success. The service awaits the RPC result and returns only\nafter both rows commit. RPC failure rolls back both writes and produces HTTP 503 detail\n`routing-durability-unavailable`; the MCP mirror returns its existing 503 error envelope.\nFire-and-forget `AuditService.log_operation()` is not used for this invariant, and neither\nan orphan decision nor an orphan audit link is observable. Existing dg-00 callers still\ntake their exact static fallback on any non-200 response.\n\nThe `routing_decisions.policy_version` column keeps dg-00 scorer version\n`linear-utility-v1`; the routing YAML version/checksum live in selected provenance. No raw\nsecret, environment value, prompt, free-form task-signal extra, or unbounded path list\nenters either record; only typed/bounded categories and rationale enter persistence.\n\n## D8 — Local fallback is configuration-derived and honest\n\nA skills-side bridge/helper may fall back only after transport timeout/unreachability. It\nloads the checkout's validated `routing.yaml`, `agents.yaml`, and archetype model map,\nthen combines the caller's already-resolved static provider/model with the fallback\ndimension order. It never embeds a roster, fabricates availability, or performs fuzzy\nassociation.\n\nThe response has the normal assignment shape plus `fallback=true`,\n`source=local-static`, `persisted=false`, `durable_audit=false`, and a bounded\nfailure reason. Its catalog key is null because no live catalog join occurred. A local\nUUID is explicitly not retrievable from coordinator decision storage. Missing or invalid\nconfiguration fails loud; the helper does not invent permissive defaults.\n\nThe fallback table's order is only a deterministic choice among the lane's exact\nconfigured values while the coordinator is unreachable. It is not an isolation-strength\nprecedence or enforcement policy. The reusable helper lives in\n`skills/coordination-bridge/scripts/routing_fallback.py`, resolves repository config from\nan explicit root or discovered checkout root, and is used by bridge and HTTP-proxy\ndegradation paths.\n\nThe existing `resolve_archetype_for_phase` fallback is not rewritten: disabled,\nfailure, malformed-response, and timeout paths still return the exact dg-00 static\n`ResolvedArchetype` object with no added reasons or fields.\n\n## D9 — DG-05/DG-06 boundaries remain closed\n\nDG-04 carries the lane's current configured isolation as data and may filter an explicit\nrequest. It does not define per-mode overrides, the isolation precedence ladder, or\nenforcement; DG-05 owns that contract. It does not call routing before `dispatch_fn`,\nchange `phase_agent.py`, redispatch work, or add loop caps; DG-06 owns obedience.\nNo sandbox is launched; DG-07 owns enforcement.\n\n## D10 — Test-first packages and validation\n\nContract/config tests fail first, followed by pure policy/association tests, then service\nand transport/fallback tests. PostgreSQL coverage proves the additive JSONB decision\nround trip and durable audit link. {"type":"message_start","message":{"role":"toolResult","toolCallId":"chatcmpl-tool-e0689e421fe34f0d9d63ab45a11571a8","toolName":"read","content":[{"type":"text","text":"# Design: extend routing to vendor × location × isolation × dispatch mode\n\n## D1 — Extend one resolver and one public operation\n\nDG-04 extends the dg-00 `RoutingService.select_model()` pipeline, HTTP\n`POST /routing/select_model`, and MCP `select_model_for_task`. It does not add\n`POST /route/task`, a second score function, or a second routing decision store.\nThe existing `selected.vendor/model/endpoint_kind` meaning remains observable and\nunchanged; assignment and provenance are additive fields.\n\n## D2 — Preserve compatibility with an optional strict profile\n\nLegacy `task_signals` remains accepted with its current permissive extra-field\nbehavior because existing phase callers send fields such as `write_allow`. A new\noptional `routing_profile` is strict (`extra=forbid`) and types:\n\n- expected duration seconds;\n- scope category (`read-only|bounded-write|broad-write`);\n- interactivity (`interactive|headless`);\n- secret need category (`none|brokered|direct`), never a secret value;\n- positive parallelism;\n- repository shape (`single-package|monorepo|unknown`);\n- roadmap-policy constraints (allowed/excluded lane/vendor sets and an allowed-location set);\n- optional required location, isolation, and dispatch mode.\n\nPydantic validates the external boundary and FastAPI/MCP share the same request model.\nNew response objects are optional-with-default for legacy validation but are always\npopulated by a successful DG-04 service decision.\n\n## D3 — Rules are ordered, typed, and versioned\n\n`agent-coordinator/routing.yaml` carries `schema_version`, `policy_version`,\ndispatch-mode defaults, ordered first-match constraint rules, and a local-fallback\ndimension table. A dedicated loader validates unknown fields, duplicate IDs, enum values,\nranges, and phase dispatch defaults, then records a SHA-256 checksum of canonical file\nbytes.\n\nEach rule has a typed `when` predicate over the profile and a typed `constrain` block for\nlocation, isolation, and dispatch mode. Explicit request constraints take precedence;\notherwise the first matching rule that mentions a dimension constrains that dimension.\nThe phase-specific or global dispatch default is used only when no explicit or rule-based\ndispatch mode exists; unmatched location/isolation remain unconstrained. Rules narrow\nfeasibility and never add a second utility score. Changing a rule therefore changes the\nfeasible assignment set without code edits.\n\nThe Docker image copies the file beside `agents.yaml` and the loader resolves it from\n`ROUTING_CONFIG` or the package root, never the process working directory.\n\n## D4 — DG-01 is the only lane source and joins are exact\n\n`RoutingService` injects/loads `VendorRegistryService` in process and requests all\nlanes without `available_only` prefiltering so exclusion provenance is retained. For\neach lane it consumes dg-01's projected catalog models. It forms an assignment only when\nthe catalog candidate identity exactly equals the projection key:\n\n`(catalog_vendor, model, endpoint_kind, base_url)`.\n\n`base_url` and additive lane identity travel through `CandidateInput` and\n`ScoredCandidate`. Agent-name suffixes, provider/publisher guesses, substring matches,\nand fuzzy model names are forbidden. Missing or ambiguous projections remain explicit\nregistry misses and never become routable candidates.\n\nA watchdog `ConfiguredCatalogSync` job materializes configured non-OpenRouter lane\nmodels in `model_catalog`. `agents.yaml` explicitly sets `catalog_vendor` and\n`endpoint_kind` for those lanes: local subscription CLIs use their exact vendor type plus\n`vendor-cli`; remote SDK lanes use their exact vendor type plus `vendor-sdk`. CLI model\nIDs come from the canonical provider model map; SDK model IDs come only from the lane's\nSDK model/fallback list. The job inserts only missing identity rows, with enabled catalog\navailability and unknown price/posterior, and never overwrites existing pricing,\nposterior, availability, or refresh data. Registry probe/rate-limit state remains the live\nlane-availability source.\n\nOpenRouter/local catalog rows remain owned by their existing refresh/probe jobs; for a\nmulti-publisher OpenRouter lane, exact model/endpoint/base-URL matching must yield one row\nbefore the row's catalog vendor becomes part of the four-field key. Missing or ambiguous\nidentity metadata is an explicit configuration miss, never filled from an agent-name\nsuffix or publisher guess. A real-agents.yaml test proves at least one configured CLI\nlane projects exactly after this bootstrap.\n\nThe routing path constructs a read-only `VendorRegistryService(audit=None)` because the\nrouter persists its own typed exclusions and atomic audit link; this avoids emitting one\ngeneric projection-miss audit row per request. The registry and catalog snapshots are\neach loaded once per request. A registry read or shape failure fails closed as\n`routing-registry-unavailable`; it never falls back to catalog-only scoring. Catalog rows\nwith no exact configured lane projection are retained in `excluded` as\n`catalog:no-configured-lane`, rather than disappearing silently.\n\n## D5 — Feasibility precedes DG-00 utility\n\nFor each exact lane/model pair, pure feasibility checks apply in deterministic order:\n\n1. live lane availability and lane/model rate limits;\n2. dispatchability, archetype, and requested/default dispatch mode;\n3. explicit/configured location and isolation constraints;\n4. roadmap-policy allow/exclude sets;\n5. catalog availability and dg-00 modality/quota constraints.\n\nReasons are machine-readable and sanitized. DG-00's existing `unavailable` and\n`quota:exhausted` values remain accepted alongside DG-04's namespaced reasons. Only feasible lane/model candidates enter\nthe existing `score_and_rank`; DG-04 does not duplicate quality, posterior, cost,\nlatency, headroom, or exploration math. Multiple lanes may project the same catalog\nmodel, so the final stable order is `(-score, agent_id, catalog identity)`.\nLocation and isolation constraints use exact equality and dispatch mode uses exact\nmembership in the lane's configured modes; DG-04 does not infer an isolation-strength\nordering.\n\n## D6 — Assignment and provenance are additive\n\nA successful response adds top-level:\n\n- `assignment`: exact `agent_id`, `vendor_type`, `policy_vendor`,\n  `catalog_vendor`, location, isolation, dispatch mode, model, endpoint kind, and base\n  URL;\n- `provenance`: source (`coordinator` or `local-static`), policy version/checksum,\n  matched rule IDs, rationale, persistence flag, durable-audit flag, and exact\n  lane/catalog key.\n\nThe selected candidate and every alternative carry their own additive `assignment`, while\nthe response retains the selected candidate's assignment/provenance at top level for\nconvenience. Existing selected-candidate fields remain intact for older consumers.\nExcluded assignments use a typed shape containing lane/catalog identity and a bounded\nmachine-readable reason.\n\n## D7 — Durable routing record is authoritative; audit event is linked\n\nThe existing `routing_decisions` row is the authoritative durable routing audit. Its\nsanitized `request` stores only declared task signals and the strict routing profile;\npermissive legacy extras such as `write_allow` are never persisted. Its `selected` object\nstores selected assignment plus provenance, and every item in `alternatives` stores its\nown assignment. `excluded` stores typed exclusion records. These are additive JSONB\nshapes and require no new table columns.\n\nMigration `042_atomic_routing_audit.sql` adds one transaction-scoped RPC that inserts the\n`routing_decisions` row and a sanitized link-only `routing_decision` audit-log event\natomically. The event contains only decision ID, selected agent/model, routing-policy\nversion/checksum, source, and success. The service awaits the RPC result and returns only\nafter both rows commit. RPC failure rolls back both writes and produces HTTP 503 detail\n`routing-durability-unavailable`; the MCP mirror returns its existing 503 error envelope.\nFire-and-forget `AuditService.log_operation()` is not used for this invariant, and neither\nan orphan decision nor an orphan audit link is observable. Existing dg-00 callers still\ntake their exact static fallback on any non-200 response.\n\nThe `routing_decisions.policy_version` column keeps dg-00 scorer version\n`linear-utility-v1`; the routing YAML version/checksum live in selected provenance. No raw\nsecret, environment value, prompt, free-form task-signal extra, or unbounded path list\nenters either record; only typed/bounded categories and rationale enter persistence.\n\n## D8 — Local fallback is configuration-derived and honest\n\nA skills-side bridge/helper may fall back only after transport timeout/unreachability. It never embeds a roster, fabricates availability, or performs fuzzy\nassociation.\n\nThe response has the normal assignment shape plus `fallback=true`,\n`source=local-static`, `persisted=false`, `durable_audit=false`, and a bounded\nfailure reason. Its catalog key is null because no live catalog join occurred. A local\nUUID is explicitly not retrievable from coordinator decision storage. Missing or invalid\nconfiguration fails loud; the helper does not invent permissive defaults.\n\nThe fallback table's order is only a deterministic choice among the lane's exact\nconfigured values while the coordinator is unreachable. It is not an isolation-strength\nprecedence or enforcement policy. The reusable helper lives in\n`skills/coordination-bridge/scripts/routing_fallback.py`, resolves repository config from\nan explicit root or discovered checkout root, and is used by bridge and HTTP-proxy\ndegradation paths.\n\nThe existing `resolve_archetype_for_phase` fallback is not rewritten: disabled,\nfailure, malformed-response, and timeout paths still return the exact dg-00 static\n`ResolvedArchetype` object with no added reasons or fields.\n\n## D9 — DG-05/DG-06 boundaries remain closed\n\nDG-04 carries the lane's current configured isolation as data and may filter an explicit\nrequest. Requirement: One additive routing surface\n\nThe coordinator SHALL extend `POST /routing/select_model` and its\n`select_model_for_task` MCP mirror with task-profile and assignment fields, and SHALL NOT\nadd a second task-routing endpoint or scoring path.\n\n#### Scenario: Existing HTTP and MCP surfaces stay aligned\n\n- **WHEN** the same valid task-routing request is submitted through HTTP and Scenario: Legacy caller remains compatible\n\n- **WHEN** a caller sends only the dg-00 `task_signals.archetype` field\n- **THEN** the request SHALL remain valid\n- **AND** newly added input and output location, isolation, or dispatch-mode constraint SHALL be\n  applied deterministically\n- **AND** the matching rule ID SHALL be recorded in decision provenance.\n\n### Requirement: Registry-backed feasibility precedes utility\n\nThe router SHALL consume `VendorRegistryService` in process and remove infeasible\nlane/model assignments before invoking the existing dg-00 utility scorer. A periodic\nconfiguration-backed job SHALL materialize missing non-OpenRouter catalog identities from\nexplicit lane metadata and the canonical provider model map without overwriting live\ncatalog observations.\n\n#### Scenario: Configured lane identity is materialized\n\n- **WHEN** a configured non-OpenRouter lane model is absent from `model_catalog`\n- **THEN** the catalog job SHALL insert posterior, availability, or refresh data.\n\n#### Scenario: Exact lane and catalog association\n\n- **WHEN** a registry lane projects a catalog model\n- **THEN** routing SHALL associate it only by the exact projected catalog vendor, model,\n  endpoint-kind, and base-URL identity\n- **AND** SHALL NOT infer association from agent ID suffixes, publisher names, or fuzzy\n  model strings.\n\n#### Scenario: Infeasible assignment cannot win\n\n- **WHEN** a lane is unavailable, rate limited, lacks the archetype or dispatch mode, or\n  violates location, isolation, or roadmap-policy constraints\n- **THEN** the lane/model assignment SHALL be excluded before dg-00 utility scoring\n- **AND** the exclusion SHALL carry a machine-readable reason.\n\n#### Scenario: Registry failure fails closed\n\n- **WHEN** the in-process registry snapshot cannot be loaded or validated\n- **THEN** routing SHALL fail with `routing-registry-unavailable`\n- **AND** SHALL NOT score catalog-only candidates or infer a lane association.\n\n#### Scenario: Unprojected catalog candidate remains explainable\n\n- **WHEN** a catalog row has no exact configured lane projection\n- **THEN** it SHALL NOT enter utility scoring\n- **AND** it SHALL appear in exclusions as `catalog:no-configured-lane`.\n\n#### Scenario: Feasible assignments retain dg-00 ranking\n\n- **WHEN** two or more lane/model assignments remain feasible\n- **THEN** their quality, cost, latency, headroom, and exploration ranking SHALL be\n  produced by the existing dg-00 scorer without a second utility function\n- **AND** equal scores SHALL be ordered by agent ID and exact catalog identity.\n\n### Requirement: Versioned deterministic routing policy\n\nRouting dimension rules SHALL be loaded from a schema-validated `routing.yaml` carrying\nan explicit schema version and policy version.\n\n#### Scenario: Policy edit changes a decision\n\n- **WHEN** a test changes a valid constraint rule or dispatch default in `routing.yaml`\n- **THEN** the resulting assignment SHALL change without a Python code edit\n- **AND** repeated evaluation of the same profile, registry snapshot, catalog snapshot,\n  and policy SHALL produce the same ordered candidates when exploration is disabled.\n\n#### Scenario: Invalid policy fails loud\n\n- **WHEN** `routing.yaml` contains an unknown field, unsupported schema version, invalid\n  enum, duplicate rule ID, or reference to an unconfigured phase dispatch default\n- **THEN** policy loading SHALL fail before routing a task\n- **AND** SHALL NOT silently substitute permissive defaults.\n\n### Requirement: Additive assignment and provenance\n\nEvery selected candidate SHALL expose exact lane assignment fields and every persisted\ndecision SHALL retain the task profile, policy version/checksum, matched rules, excluded\nassignments, and source.\n\n#### Scenario: Coordinator decision is durable and auditable\n\n- **WHEN** the coordinator returns a routing decision\n- **THEN** the same decision ID and assignment SHALL be written to `routing_decisions`\n- **AND** a link-only coordinator audit event SHALL record decision ID, selected\n  agent/model, routing-policy version/checksum, source, and success\n- **AND** both records SHALL commit atomically before the response is returned.\n\n#### Scenario: Durable write cannot be established\n\n- **WHEN** the atomic decision-and-audit RPC fails\n- **THEN** neither record SHALL remain committed\n- **AND** HTTP SHALL return 503 detail `routing-durability-unavailable`\n- **AND** MCP SHALL return its existing matching 503 error envelope.\n\n#### Scenario: Persistence projection is bounded\n\n- **WHEN** permissive legacy task signals include undeclared values such as path lists\n- **THEN** the request remains valid for compatibility\n- **AND** persistence SHALL retain only declared task signals and the typed routing\n  profile, excluding all legacy extras.\n\n#### Scenario: Alternative candidates endpoint kind, and base URL.\n\n### Requirement: Honest local fallback\n\nA coordinator-unreachable client path SHALL derive a deterministic assignment only from\nthe checkout's validated `routing.yaml`, `agents.yaml`, archetype model map, and caller's\nstatic model/provider inputs.\n\n#### Scenario: Coordinator is unreachable\n\n- **WHEN** the coordinator routing operation times out This is fine.\n\nLet me check the VendorLane from dg-01: it has `catalog_vendor` as optional (nullable). The design D4 says \"For each lane it consumes dg-01's projected catalog models. It forms an assignment only when the catalog candidate identity exactly equals the projection key: (catalog_vendor, model, endpoint_kind, base_url).\" But if catalog_vendor is nullable in VendorLane, how does this work? The design says \"OpenRouter/local catalog rows remain owned by their existing refresh/probe jobs; for a multi-publisher OpenRouter lane, exact model/endpoint/base-URL matching must yield one row before the row's catalog vendor becomes part of the four-field key.\" So for OpenRouter lanes, the catalog_vendor comes from the catalog row, not from the lane config. For non-OpenRouter lanes, the lane should have catalog_vendor set explicitly in agents.yaml.\n\nThe design also says: \"agents.yaml explicitly sets catalog_vendor and endpoint_kind for those lanes: local subscription CLIs use their exact vendor type plus vendor-cli; remote SDK lanes use their exact vendor type plus vendor-sdk.\" So this is addressed.\n\nNow let me look for potential issues:\n\n1. **routing.yaml fallback missing dispatch_mode** - The schema only has location_order and isolation_order in fallback. The design says fallback uses \"the lane's exact configured values\" but dispatch_mode is not in the fallback ordering. This could be a gap since dispatch_mode is a routing dimension.\n\n2. **The openapi v1.1 Candidate.assignment requires `catalog_vendor` but the dg-01 VendorLane has `catalog_vendor` as nullable** - The assignment schema requires catalog_vendor (it's in required array). But if a lane doesn't have catalog_vendor set (like OpenRouter lanes), how is this handled? The design says for OpenRouter, the catalog_vendor comes from the catalog row match. So it should be populated at routing time. This seems fine.\n\n3. **The routing-decision.schema.json has `source` with const \"coordinator\" and `success` with const true** - This means the audit event only represents successful coordinator decisions. The design says the RPC is atomic and only commits on success. Failed decisions don't create audit events (they return 503). Local fallback doesn't create audit events. This seems correct per design.\n\n4. **Work-packages.yaml wp-policy-service locks `agent-coordinator/src/vendor_registry.py` and `agent-coordinator/src/watchdog.py`** - These are dg-01 files. Since dg-04 depends on dg-01, modifying dg-01 files in dg-04 could be a coupling concern. But the design says the ConfiguredCatalogSync job goes in watchdog.py and the RoutingService uses VendorRegistryService in-process. The watchdog.py changes are for the new job. The vendor_registry.py might need changes to support the in-process usage pattern. This is a cross-cutting concern but may be acceptable.\n\n5. **The design D4 says \"The routing path constructs a read-only VendorRegistryService(audit=None)\"** - This creates a new instance without audit. The VendorRegistryService from dg-01 might not support audit=None parameter. This is an implementation detail but could be a compatibility issue.\n\n6. **The openapi v1.1 SelectModelRequest has `routing_profile` as optional with default null** - But the design says \"A new optional routing_profile is strict (extra=forbid)\". The schema has `additionalProperties: false` on TaskRoutingProfile, which is good. But the routing_profile itself is optional at the request level. This is fine for backward compatibility.\n\n7. **The work-packages.yaml wp-contract-config has `role: contracts-author` but no `archetype`** - Other packages have `archetype: implementer` or `archetype: validator`. This might be intentional since it's a contracts package.\n\n8. **The design D7 says \"The routing_decisions.policy_version column keeps dg-00 scorer version linear-utility-v1; the routing YAML version/checksum live in selected provenance.\"** - This means the database column policy_version is NOT updated to include routing policy version. The routing policy version/checksum is only in the provenance JSONB. This is a design decision that should be explicit. It could be a finding if it's not clearly communicated.\n\n9. **The tasks.md task 1.5 says \"Pin bounded persistence projection, typed exclusions, and exact local-fallback invariants in contracts.\"** - The contracts seem to cover this.\n\n10. **The spec.md says \"A periodic configuration-backed job SHALL materialize missing non-OpenRouter catalog identities from explicit lane metadata and the canonical provider model map without overwriting live catalog observations.\"** - This is the ConfiguredCatalogSync job. The design D4 describes it. The work-packages.yaml includes watchdog.py in wp-policy-service scope. This seems covered.\n\n11. **The openapi v1.1 ExcludedAssignment reason pattern includes `cedar:` prefix** - This is a dg-00 reason. The design says \"DG-00's existing unavailable and quota:exhausted values remain accepted alongside DG-04's namespaced reasons.\" The pattern allows `(lane|policy|catalog|roadmap|registry|cedar):`. This seems correct.\n\n12. **The routing.yaml schema rule.when has minProperties: 1 but no required fields** - This means a rule could have just `phase` or just `scope`, etc. The design says \"Each rule has a typed when predicate over the profile and a typed constrain block\". This seems intentional for flexibility.\n\n13. **The work-packages.yaml wp-integration has `locks: {files: [], keys: [\"feature:task-routing:integration\"]}`** - Empty files lock but a key lock. This is fine for an integration package.\n\n14. **The design D3 says \"The Docker image copies the file beside agents.yaml and the loader resolves it from ROUTING_CONFIG or the package root, never the process working directory.\"** - This is good practice.\n\n15. **The spec.md requirement \"Honest local fallback\" says \"its catalog key SHALL be null because no live catalog join occurred\"** - The openapi RoutingProvenance has catalog_key as nullable array or null. This matches.\n\n16. **The spec.md requirement \"Additive assignment and provenance\" says \"the same decision ID and assignment SHALL be written to routing_decisions\" and \"a link-only coordinator audit event SHALL record decision ID, selected agent/model, routing-policy version/checksum, source, and success\" and \"both records SHALL commit atomically before the response is returned\"** - The design D7 covers this with migration 042 and atomic RPC.\n\n17. **The spec.md requirement \"Registry-backed feasibility precedes utility\" says \"Registry failure fails closed\" and \"Unprojected catalog candidate remains explainable\"** - The design D4 and D5 cover this.\n\nNow, let me identify actual findings that are issues or gaps:\n\n**Finding 1**: The `routing.schema.json` fallback section only defines `location_order` and `isolation_order` but not `dispatch_mode_order`. Since dispatch_mode is a routing dimension (along with location and isolation), the fallback should have a deterministic order for dispatch_mode as well, or explicitly document why it's omitted (e.g., it comes from phase defaults). The design D8 says \"The fallback table's order is only a deterministic choice among the lane's exact configured values\" - this implies all three dimensions. This is a spec_gap.\n\n**Finding 2**: The `routing-decision.schema.json` audit event has `source` with `const: \"coordinator\"` and `success` with `const: true`. This schema cannot represent failed routing decisions or local fallback decisions. While the design says failed decisions return 503 and don't create audit events, and local fallback doesn't create audit events, having a schema that only allows success=true and source=coordinator limits observability. If the requirement is \"honestly linked durable coordinator audit event\", the schema should at least allow success=false for failed atomic commits, or this should be explicitly documented as intentional. This is a potential observability gap.\n\n**Finding 3**: The `wp-policy-service` package locks `agent-coordinator/src/vendor_registry.py` and `agent-coordinator/src/watchdog.py` which are dg-01 files. Since dg-04 is stacked on dg-01, modifying dg-01 files in dg-04 creates a coupling that could complicate merging and testing. The design says \"RoutingService injects/loads VendorRegistryService in process\" - if this requires changes to vendor_registry.py (e.g., adding audit=None constructor parameter), that's a dg-01 interface change. This is an architecture/compatibility concern.\n\n**Finding 4**: The openapi v1.1 `Candidate` schema has `assignment` and `provenance` as optional with default null, but the design says \"New response objects are optional-with-default for legacy validation but are always populated by a successful DG-04 service decision.\" The schema allows null, which is correct for backward compatibility, but there's no way to enforce at the schema level that successful decisions always populate these. This is a runtime guarantee only. This is fine but worth noting as a design choice.\n\n**Finding 5**: The `routing.yaml` schema validation happens in a \"dedicated loader\" (design D3) rather than purely in JSON schema. The JSON schema validates structure but not semantic constraints like \"phase_dispatch_modes references valid phases\" or \"rule IDs are unique\". The design says the loader validates these. This is an implementation concern but the plan should specify that the loader is part of the contract. The tasks.md task 1.3 says \"Define and validate versioned routing.yaml\" - this covers it.\n\n**Finding 6**: The design D4 says \"The routing path constructs a read-only VendorRegistryService(audit=None) because the router persists its own typed exclusions and atomic audit link; this avoids emitting one generic projection-miss audit row per request.\" This implies VendorRegistryService accepts an `audit` parameter. If dg-01's VendorRegistryService doesn't have this parameter, this is a breaking change to dg-01. This needs verification against dg-01's actual interface.\n\n**Finding 7**: The work-packages.yaml has `wp-contract-config` with `role: contracts-author` but no `archetype` field, while other packages have `archetype: implementer` or `archetype: validator`. This might be intentional but could be an inconsistency in the package definition schema.\n\n**Finding 8**: The design D7 says \"The routing_decisions.policy_version column keeps dg-00 scorer version linear-utility-v1; the routing YAML version/checksum live in selected provenance.\" This means the database column `policy_version` is overloaded - it stores the scorer version, not the routing policy version. The routing policy version is only in the provenance JSONB. This could be confusing for queries and should be explicitly called out as a design decision. The migration 042 should document this.\n\n**Finding 9**: The openapi v1.1 `SelectModelRequest` has `task_signals` with `additionalProperties: true` (permissive for legacy) and `routing_profile` with `additionalProperties: false` (strict). But there's no validation that `routing_profile` is provided when the caller wants the new routing dimensions. The design says it's optional. This is fine.\n\n**Finding 10**: The spec.md says \"Config rules consume typed signals\" and \"the matching rule ID SHALL be recorded in decision provenance.\" The openapi `RoutingProvenance` has `matched_rule_ids` array. This is covered.\n\nLet me now formulate the findings with proper JSON format. A dedicated loader validates unknown fields, duplicate IDs, enum values,\nranges, and phase dispatch defaults, then records a SHA-256 checksum of canonical file\nbytes.\n\nEach rule has a typed `when` predicate over the profile and a typed `constrain` block for\nlocation, isolation, and dispatch mode. The design says the RPC is atomic and only commits on success. Failed decisions don't create audit events (they return 503). Local fallback doesn't create audit events. This seems correct per design.\n\n4. **Work-packages.yaml wp-policy-service locks `agent-coordinator/src/vendor_registry.py` and `agent-coordinator/src/watchdog.py`** - These are dg-01 files. Since dg-04 depends on dg-01, modifying dg-01 files in dg-04 could be a coupling concern. But the design says the ConfiguredCatalogSync job goes in watchdog.py and the RoutingService uses VendorRegistryService in-process. The watchdog.py changes are for the new job. The vendor_registry.py might need changes to support the in-process usage pattern. This is a cross-cutting concern but may be acceptable.\n\n5. **The design D4 says \"The routing path constructs a read-only VendorRegistryService(audit=None)\"** - This creates a new instance without audit. The VendorRegistryService from dg-01 might not support audit=None parameter. This is an implementation detail but could be a compatibility issue.\n\n6. **The openapi v1.1 SelectModelRequest has `routing_profile` as optional with default null** - But the design says \"A new optional routing_profile is strict (extra=forbid)\". The schema has `additionalProperties: false` on TaskRoutingProfile, which is good. But the routing_profile itself is optional at the request level. This is fine for backward compatibility.\n\n7. **The work-packages.yaml wp-contract-config has `role: contracts-author` but no `archetype`** - Other packages have `archetype: implementer` or `archetype: validator`. The routing policy version/checksum is only in the provenance JSONB. This is a design decision that should be explicit. This seems covered.\n\n11. **The openapi v1.1 ExcludedAssignment reason pattern includes `cedar:` prefix** - This is a dg-00 reason. This seems correct.\n\n12. **The routing.yaml schema rule.when has minProperties: 1 but no required fields** - This means a rule could have just `phase` or just `scope`, etc. The design says \"Each rule has a typed when predicate over the profile and a typed constrain block\". This is fine for an integration package.\n\n14. **The design D3 says \"The Docker image copies the file beside agents.yaml and the loader resolves it from ROUTING_CONFIG or the package root, never the process working directory.\"** - This is good practice.\n\n15. **The spec.md requirement \"Honest local fallback\" says \"its catalog key SHALL be null because no live catalog join occurred\"** - The openapi RoutingProvenance has catalog_key as nullable array or null.
